notes.meaning: Jesus announces that spiritual life is now being given through his voice. People who are dead in their sins hear the message of Christ and are made alive through faith. This shows the divine power of his word to save sinners right now.

differ.view: Christ speaks here specifically of the elect, whose ears and hearts God graciously opens so that they can hear his voice and receive life.

notes.meaning: God the Father possesses life within himself and does not depend on anyone else to exist. He has granted his Son to have that same self-existent life, so Jesus can give life to whoever hears him.

The Father has appointed Jesus with full authority to act as the final judge over the world. Because Jesus became a human being, he is uniquely suited to judge humanity with perfect fairness and mercy.

Jesus tells his listeners not to be astonished, because a day is coming when all the dead will hear his voice and rise from their graves. Those who have trusted God and lived righteously will rise to everlasting life, while those who persisted in wicked rebellion will rise to face condemnation.

differ.view: Good works do not earn eternal life, but they serve as the necessary fruit that distinguishes true believers from the condemned.

notes.meaning: Jesus explains that he never acts alone or seeks a private agenda apart from his Father. His judgments are completely fair because he simply carries out the exact will of God who sent him.
Under Jewish law, a person could not win a legal case on their own unsupported word. Jesus acknowledges this rule of evidence, agreeing that his claims need proper witnesses beside himself.
Jesus points out that there is another witness who speaks on his behalf, namely God the Father. Jesus knows that the Father's witness is completely reliable and impossible to disprove.
The religious leaders had sent an official group to question John the Baptist. John faithfully spoke the truth to them by pointing directly to Jesus as the Messiah.
Jesus does not need human testimony to prove who he is or to confirm his divine mission. He reminds his listeners of John's words only so they might believe the truth and be saved.

John the Baptist was like a lamp that burned brightly and helped people see the truth for a time. The crowds were glad to enjoy his preaching for a little while, but they failed to welcome the Savior he introduced.
Jesus has a far greater witness than any human prophet could provide. The miracles he performs and the work his Father gave him to finish clearly prove that he was sent by God.
The Father who sent Jesus has directly testified about him through prophecies and at his baptism. Yet the religious leaders had never truly recognized God's voice or known what he was like.
God's message had never found a true home in the hearts of these leaders. Their refusal to trust Jesus, whom the Father sent, showed that they did not truly hold God's word inside them.

The leaders studied the Scriptures with great care, thinking that the mere possession of the holy books would give them eternal life. Yet all those ancient writings were designed to point people directly to Jesus.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars understand the first word as a statement about what the leaders were already doing ('You search the Scriptures') rather than a command to study.

notes.meaning: Even though the Scriptures point directly to Christ, the leaders stubbornly refused to come to him. True spiritual life is found only in Jesus, but their hard hearts kept them from receiving it.
Jesus does not look for praise, honors, or approval from human beings. His claims are not driven by personal ambition or a desire to gain a popular following.
Jesus knew the secret thoughts and motives of his opponents with complete clarity. Despite all their outward religious observance, they did not have any real love for God in their hearts.

Jesus came acting on his Father's authority and doing his Father's work, but the leaders rejected him. Yet if an impostor came speaking on his own authority to promote himself, they would gladly welcome him.

Genuine faith was impossible for these leaders because they were consumed with seeking praise and status from one another. Caring only about human opinions blinded them to the true honor that comes from God alone.
Jesus did not need to step forward as their prosecutor before the Father. Moses himself, whose law they claimed to trust for their salvation, was already the one accusing them of disobedience.

Moses wrote about the coming Savior throughout the first five books of the Bible. If the leaders had truly believed what Moses wrote, they would have recognized and believed in Jesus without hesitation.

The leaders claimed Moses as their highest authority, yet they refused to accept the clear message of his writings. Since they did not believe what Moses wrote down, it was no surprise that they rejected what Jesus said.
